relations.note: The Maruts are repeatedly called Rudra’s sons and share his fierceness and medicines.
Pṛśni bears or mothers the Maruts as their cow-like dappled maternal figure.

relations.myth: Indra and the Maruts battle Vṛtra
relations.note: The Maruts sing for, strengthen, and accompany Indra in defeating Vṛtra and releasing the waters.
They dispute Indra’s exclusive claim to victory, assert their power, then praise and reconcile with him.
The Maruts and Indra contend over ritual allegiance or shares before an urged reconciliation.
Indra cuts Diti’s fetus into seven pieces, then grants the surviving Maruts divine stations.
Indra divides Diti’s embryo into seven groups of seven, producing forty-nine Maruts.
The surviving Maruts address Indra as brother and are admitted among the gods.
After dividing the embryo, Indra grants the Maruts divine status and accepts them as allies.

relations.myth: Indra and the Maruts battle Vṛtra
relations.note: The Maruts assist Indra against Vṛtra and help enable the release of the waters.

relations.myth: Agni comes surrounded by the Maruts
relations.note: Agni and the Maruts are jointly invoked as cooperating ritual and atmospheric powers.
The Maruts receive and drink Soma, whose exhilaration accompanies their mighty deeds.
A difficult Ṛgvedic expression associates Viṣṇu with the Maruts, though the precise relationship remains disputed.
Viṣṇu’s favor makes Diti’s divided embryos indestructible and permits their elevation as gods.
Diti conceives the embryo that becomes seven Marut groups after Indra divides it.
Diti’s divided embryo becomes forty-nine Maruts in the elaborated Purāṇic genealogy.
Kaśyapa fathers Diti’s pregnancy, from which the seven Marut groups arise.
Kaśyapa fathers Diti’s pregnancy and prescribes the vow preceding the Maruts’ birth.
As Diti’s sister and Indra’s mother, Aditi is the Maruts’ aunt in later genealogy.
The Maruts join the gods in praising Devī and celebrating her defeat of the Asuras.
Epic and Purāṇic divine armies include the Maruts among the hosts surrounding Skanda.
Sātyaki is presented as a heroic incarnation connected with a portion of the Maruts.
